evidence.heading: Setup
evidence.text:
1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
2. Remove destiny cards naming unused player colors; shuffle the rest, including wilds and specials.
3. Shuffle the flares, deal two to each player, and give them the matching alien sheets. Each secretly chooses one alien, initially placing it facedown, and returns the other sheet to the box. This is the standard selection procedure; Hidden Powers is a separate excluded variant. The original text does not specify when standard-game sheets are turned faceup; unlike the optional Hidden Powers rule, it gives no explicit reveal window. This source gap is recorded rather than supplying a new setup rule. Green/yellow/red indicate recommended experience, not strength. Beginners may start with green aliens without flares.
4. Add **both flares dealt to every player**, including rejected aliens' flares, to the cosmic deck. Add random extras if needed to reach ten flares total; shuffle. Deal eight-card hands. Keep card faces private unless an effect allows showing them.
5. Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle the drawn card back into the destiny deck. Play passes left thereafter.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Card information, discards and exhaustion
evidence.text: If the cosmic deck runs out, reshuffle available discards. If a needed draw has no deck or discards, a **Cosmic Quake** makes everyone discard their hands; shuffle and deal eight to each player. If still insufficient, **Cosmic Aftershock** gathers all cosmic cards, including Miser's hoard and other set-aside cards, shuffles them, and replenishes Game Setup card holdings as at setup (including Miser's hoard). This is a needed-draw exhaustion rule, not an optional hand refresh.

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text: This summary covers the original **Fantasy Flight English 2008 CE01** game for 3–5 players, including its fifty original aliens, normal flare system and applicable official FAQ rulings. Optional Technology, Four Planets, Hidden Powers, Rotating Powers and Freewheeling Flares are excluded, as are Anniversary bonus content and all expansions. Read an individual card's printed effect and timing when playing it; the flare rules below explain the shared system rather than reproduce every flare card.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Reincarnator
evidence.text: **FAQ p19; retained official May6 2009 FAQ p1:** The Reincarnator flare's corrected timing is after the end of the encounter, so it does not stop a same-phase power use during the encounter. Its Wild targets another player, never yourself. You cannot use the Super flares of your incarnations. Corrected Wild: after another player besides Reincarnator loses or fails a deal, you may give them this flare. clauses: What counts as one colony, can several players have colonies on one planet, and do five foreign colonies have to be in different systems?

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text: Each player leads an alien trying to establish five **foreign colonies**. A colony is one or more ships of one color on one planet; extra ships on that planet do not make extra colonies. Several colors can coexist there, each with its own colony. Home colonies are in your own system; foreign colonies are outside it. Five foreign planets can all be in one other system. Alien powers override conflicting general rules.

evidence.heading: Actions / Flare system
evidence.text: Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. evidence.heading: Setup
evidence.text:
1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
2. Remove destiny cards naming unused player colors; shuffle the rest, including wilds and specials.
3. Shuffle the flares, deal two to each player, and give them the matching alien sheets. Each secretly chooses one alien, initially placing it facedown, and returns the other sheet to the box. This is the standard selection procedure; Hidden Powers is a separate excluded variant. The original text does not specify when standard-game sheets are turned faceup; unlike the optional Hidden Powers rule, it gives no explicit reveal window. This source gap is recorded rather than supplying a new setup rule. Green/yellow/red indicate recommended experience, not strength. Beginners may start with green aliens without flares.
4. Add **both flares dealt to every player**, including rejected aliens' flares, to the cosmic deck. Add random extras if needed to reach ten flares total; shuffle. Deal eight-card hands. Keep card faces private unless an effect allows showing them.
5. Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle the drawn card back into the destiny deck. Play passes left thereafter.

evidence.heading: Actions / Flare system
evidence.text: Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. evidence.heading: Turn Structure / Start Turn and hand replacement
evidence.text: At Planning, a defense lacking encounter cards reveals/discards the remainder and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card. An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns its committed ships to its own colonies; each ally returns that ally's committed ships to that ally's own colonies. The normal no-colony relocation rule applies. There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards. Alien and card effects can grant different draws.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 2. Destiny
evidence.text:
- Another player's color: encounter that player in their home system.
- Your own color: redraw, or target one chosen foreign colony in your home system, making its owner the defense. Other colonies there are bystanders. This counts as a win and successful encounter, proceeds only through Launch, and can qualify you for a second encounter.
- Wild: choose another player and encounter them in their home system.
- Special: follow its conditions, defense and location. The original rulebook's illustrated special card chooses the other player with the most current foreign colonies, excluding offense. Break a tie toward offense's left, choosing the first tied eligible player there; encounter that player in their home system (rulebook p7). For color-dependent effects such as Shadow, treat it as the designated defense's color.

When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.
